For example, we study the weakly cotorsion property of $\Ext(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadratic $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$

papers.title: Peer Prediction for Learning Agents
papers.abstract: Peer prediction refers to a collection of mechanisms for eliciting information from human agents when direct verification of the obtained information is unavailable. They are designed to have a game-theoretic equilibrium where everyone reveals their private information truthfully. This result holds under the assumption that agents are Bayesian and they each adopt a fixed strategy across all tasks. Human agents however are observed in many domains to exhibit learning behavior in sequential settings. In this paper, we explore the dynamics of sequential peer prediction mechanisms when participants are learning agents. We first show that the notion of no regret alone for the agents' learning algorithms cannot guarantee convergence to the truthful strategy. We then focus on a family of learning algorithms where strategy updates only depend on agents' cumulative rewards and prove that agents' strategies in the popular Correlated Agreement (CA) mechanism converge to truthful reporting when they use algorithms from this family satisfying an additional condition on full exploitation. This family of algorithms is not necessarily no-regret, but includes fixed-parameter versions of familiar online learning algorithms (e.g multiplicative weight update and Follow the Perturbed Leader) as special cases. Simulation of several algorithms in this family as well as the $ε$-greedy algorithm, which is outside of this family, illustrates their finite-horizon behavior in the CA mechanism.

papers.title: Variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss unpolarized, complex variation of Hodge structures for non-Kähler manifolds. In particular, consider a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds with central fiber $X$. Suppose that the inclusion of complexes $(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\hookrightarrow (A^\bullet(X),d)$ induces injective maps \[ H^j(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\longrightarrow H^j(A^\bullet(X),d),\qquad j=k,\ k+1. \] Under this condition, we show that the period map is holomorphic and transversal. An essential ingredient for the proof is a deformation theory of filtered $(p,q)$-forms. We prove a jumping formula for filtered de Rham cohomology and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for its dimension to be invariant under deformation of complex structures.

papers.title: A proof of P != NP (New symmetric encryption algorithm against any linear attacks and differential attacks)
papers.abstract: P vs NP problem is the most important unresolved problem in the field of computational complexity. Its impact has penetrated into all aspects of algorithm design, especially in the field of cryptography. The security of cryptographic algorithms based on short keys depends on whether P is equal to NP. In fact, the security requirements for cryptographic keys are much stricter than those for P$\neq$NP, the security of the key must ensure not only a sufficiently high computational complexity to crack it, but also consider the security of each bit of the key, while fully avoiding the effectiveness of various attack methods. In this paper, we innovatively propose a new encoding mechanism and develop a novel block symmetric encryption algorithm, whose encryption and decryption can be completed in linear time. The key consists of 12 variables, for the attacker, in the case when only the plaintext-ciphertext correspondence is known, the problem of cracking the key is equivalent to solving a system of equations about 12 unknown variables $(w_{1}, w_{2}, ..., w_{11}, w_{12})$ together with some implicit variables which are generated by the encryption process. In this paper, we will prove that there is no universal algorithm without brute-force searching at least one variable during the process of verifying five variables $(w_{1}$, $w_{2}$, $w_{3}$, $w_{4}$, $w_{9})$ whose computational complexity is not greater than solving the 12 variables......

papers.title: Testing the number of common factors by bootstrapped sample covariance matrix in high-dimensional factor models and errata
papers.abstract: This paper studies the impact of bootstrap procedure on the eigenvalue distributions of the sample covariance matrix under a high-dimensional factor structure. We provide asymptotic distributions for the top eigenvalues of bootstrapped sample covariance matrix under mild conditions. After bootstrap, the spiked eigenvalues which are driven by common factors will converge weakly to Gaussian limits after proper scaling and centralization. However, the largest non-spiked eigenvalue is mainly determined by the order statistics of the bootstrap resampling weights, and follows extreme value distribution. Based on the disparate behavior of the spiked and non-spiked eigenvalues, we propose innovative methods to test the number of common factors. Indicated by extensive numerical and empirical studies, the proposed methods perform reliably and convincingly under the existence of both weak factors and cross-sectionally correlated errors. Our technical details contribute to random matrix theory on spiked covariance model with convexly decaying density and unbounded support, or with general elliptical distributions.

papers.title: Exploring Sequence Feature Alignment for Domain Adaptive Detection Transformers
papers.abstract: Detection transformers have recently shown promising object detection results and attracted increasing attention. However, how to develop effective domain adaptation techniques to improve its cross-domain performance remains unexplored and unclear. In this paper, we delve into this topic and empirically find that direct feature distribution alignment on the CNN backbone only brings limited improvements, as it does not guarantee domain-invariant sequence features in the transformer for prediction. To address this issue, we propose a novel Sequence Feature Alignment (SFA) method that is specially designed for the adaptation of detection transformers. Technically, SFA consists of a domain query-based feature alignment (DQFA) module and a token-wise feature alignment (TFA) module. In DQFA, a novel domain query is used to aggregate and align global context from the token sequence of both domains. DQFA reduces the domain discrepancy in global feature representations and object relations when deploying in the transformer encoder and decoder, respectively. Meanwhile, TFA aligns token features in the sequence from both domains, which reduces the domain gaps in local and instance-level feature representations in the transformer encoder and decoder, respectively. Besides, a novel bipartite matching consistency loss is proposed to enhance the feature discriminability for robust object detection. Experiments on three challenging benchmarks show that SFA outperforms state-of-the-art domain adaptive object detection methods. Code has been made available at: https://github.com/encounter1997/SFA.

papers.title: Finite Automata Encoding Piecewise Polynomials
papers.abstract: Finite automata are used to encode geometric figures and functions. The original approach is to represent each point of a figure in $\mathbb{R}^n$ as a convolution of its $n$ coordinates written in some base. Then a figure is said to be encoded as a finite automaton if the set of convolutions corresponding to the points in this figure is accepted by a Büchi automaton. The only differentiable functions which can be encoded as a finite automaton in this way are linear. This paper proposes a discretization of the original approach in which we change points as building blocks of a function to hierarchical tensor product B-splines. This reduces an uncountable set of points representing a function to a countable set of splines that enables us to use finite automata instead of Büchi automata. Moreover, it allows to represent a rich family of piecewise polynomial functions with arbitrary degrees of smoothness that can approximate any continuous functions defined on a compact domain arbitrarily close. We consider such piecewise polynomial functions with unbounded support and demonstrate that finite automata allow to handle computational tasks arising in the framework of hierarchical splines in polynomial time.

papers.title: On the fractional Dehn twist coefficients of branched coverings
papers.abstract: We discuss how the fractional Dehn twist coefficient behaves under a fully ramified branched covering of an open book, and give applications to both topological and contact 3-manifolds. Among them, we show that non-right-veering closed braids represent virtually loose transverse links.

papers.title: Measuring Information Burden: From Coalition-Based Reasoning to the Price System
papers.abstract: The price system is often said to economize on what individuals need to know. This paper measures a particular informational burden associated with decentralized reasoning in its absence: the coalition-feasibility information required for individual rejection decisions to recover the core. We develop a proof-theoretic framework in which information is represented by economically meaningful sentences and reasoning by derivations in Gentzen's sequent calculus. An agent rejects a proposed payoff vector only when she can establish the existence of a profitable coalitional deviation; failure to reject may instead reflect ignorance. For each transferable-utility game, the main theorem characterizes the informational distributions under which the set of unopposed payoff vectors coincides with the core: every noncore payoff vector must have a blocking coalition known to at least one of its members. This yields a game-specific measure of minimum informational burden. We extend the characterization to pure-exchange economies through a first-order framework that preserves finite informational premises. Applying the result to Shapley's (1975) replica economy, within the core-convergence tradition of Debreu and Scarf (1963), we show that the minimum average coalition-level informational burden grows as $Θ(4^k/k^{3/2})$, exponentially with replication. The result quantifies an informational requirement of direct decentralized coalitional reasoning that price-mediated coordination can spare agents, without claiming to measure the total informational savings of prices.

papers.title: Iterative Refinement of A Modified Lavrentiev Regularization Method for De-convolution of the Discrete Helmholtz Type Differential Filter
papers.abstract: We analyze an iterated, modified Lavrentiev regularization method (Mitlar) for deconvolving the Helmholtz-type differential filter $G=(I-δ^2Δ)^{-1}$ used in large eddy simulation. The method replaces the Lavrentiev operator $G+αI$ by the convex combination $(1-α)G+αI$; each step costs one Helmholtz solve, exactly as in iterated Lavrentiev regularization. We show that this one-line change has a precise structural meaning: the regularized operator is again a Helmholtz filter, now with the smaller radius $\sqrtα\,δ$, and $J$ refinement steps coincide with van Cittert approximate deconvolution of order $J$ applied to that filter. Consequently the regularization error is governed by the product $αδ^2$ rather than by $α$ alone. We prove sharp error bounds of order $(αδ^2)^{s}$ on a Hilbert scale, $0\le s\le J+1$, with saturation exactly at $s=J+1$; show that for noise-free data the Mitlar error never exceeds the iterated Lavrentiev error, for every datum, every $α$ and every $J$; give a priori parameter choices for noisy data with explicit $δ$-dependence; and prove finite element error bounds whose constants grow only linearly in $J$. Finally we show that the iterates decrease a natural energy functional for every $α>0$, and derive a computable stopping rule that guarantees monotone decrease of a weighted error and always terminates. Numerical examples illustrate the theory and compare Mitlar with a family of Tikhonov--Lavrentiev methods.

papers.title: A Family-Level Graphical Gatekeeping Procedure with Iterative Retesting
papers.abstract: Confirmatory clinical trials often involve multiple objectives grouped into families according to scientific priorities. At the intersection of graphical multiple testing and gatekeeping methods, we develop a Bonferroni-based family-level graphical procedure with partial-rejection-based transfers and iterative re-testing. Families are tested sequentially within each stage, using fixed component tests and a prespecified transition matrix. The updating rule combines current-stage forward contributions based on current family levels with previous-stage backward contributions based on initial allocations. We establish strong global familywise error rate control at a prespecified level under arbitrary dependence. The construction permits backward feedback while retaining fixed component tests and transition coefficients, distinguishing its implementation from forward-only family-level procedures and the specified superchain algorithm. Simulations demonstrate gains over the corresponding No-retest procedure, while identifying an efficiency cost relative to a hypothesis-level graphical comparator with matched initial allocations and edge weights. Clinical illustrations show how the procedure implements family-level priorities and feedback, and an extension accommodates a two-layer structure with multiple families per layer.

papers.title: Reductive group actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study rationality properties of reductive group actions over fields k of characteristic zero. In doing so, we unify Luna's theory of spherical systems with the Borel-Tits theory of reductive groups. Specifically, for any reductive group action, we define a generalized Tits index; its main constituents are a root system and a generalization of the anisotropic kernel. For k-spherical varieties (i.e., those for which a minimal parabolic subgroup has an open orbit), we obtain explicit smooth completions of the set of rational points. Over local fields, this yields genuine compactifications that generalize the maximal Satake compactification of symmetric spaces. Our main tool is a k-version of the Local Structure Theorem.

papers.title: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at clean and disordered quantum transitions
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields exhibits a continuous critical point, a mixed-order transition line and, with quenched disorder, an infinite-disorder fixed point and reentrant order. Using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group, we examine what the zeroth persistent homology of staggered ground-state correlations adds to conventional responses. Its barcode records the merge scales of the single-linkage hierarchy, and the maximum of its persistence-landscape velocity defines a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with an accuracy comparable to conventional responses. In the reentrant regime, the global velocity misplaces the entry, which is recovered only by restricting the filtration to the ordering scale, and none of the tested estimators locates the exit. A domain wall forced by the boundary conditions suppresses the disorder-averaged reentrant lobe. For individual disordered realizations, the labelled merge tree recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters, including noncontiguous ones missed by lattice-restricted hierarchies, with increasing agreement at stronger disorder. This information resides in the full correlation matrix, while zeroth homology provides a stable, threshold-free hierarchy.

papers.title: Selecting and verifying load-bearing periodic cells for elastic-wave band gaps with numerical acceptance checks
papers.abstract: A lattice mount must be stiff enough to support equipment and block vibration over a specified frequency range. Fast simulations help rank designs, but their errors can lead to a wrong acceptance decision. We present AMM (AgenticMetamaterials), an open-source Python tool that searches repeating cubic cells for targets on stiffness, the fraction of the cell that is solid, and band gaps. A complete band gap is an interval with no elastic-wave propagation in any direction. A separate checker allows for changes as the simulation grid gets finer. For gaps, it also tests for modes at sampled wave directions and wavelengths, so it can miss modes between samples. In 1,500 near-threshold tests of stiffness and solid fraction, the checker accepted 454 of 750 claims supported by the reference and none of the 750 false claims. Using the finest grid estimate alone accepted 42 false claims. In an independent finite-element comparison on ten new cells built from cubes joined by bars, the checker accepted one of two true gap claims and left all 17 false claims undecided. The reference could not classify the remaining claim. The protocol required every reported edge to err on the side of a narrower gap. The checker failed this test when it placed one upper edge too high, even though it left that thin-bar cell's claim undecided. Separating search from acceptance shows which targets the evidence supports and where a calculation needs further refinement.

papers.title: Model Checking Probabilistic Multiparty Session Types
papers.abstract: Distributed systems increasingly rely on randomisation; yet, verification techniques for such systems remain separate from the programming abstractions used to build them. This paper proposes the first probabilistic extension of general multiparty session types - typing sessions bottom-up, with no global specification - deriving quantitative properties of a multiparty session from its session types alone. Our types combine probabilistic choice with nondeterministic choice that abstracts data-dependent control, and allow separated choices, where each branch of a selection or branching may involve a different participant - a combination beyond previous probabilistic multiparty session type systems. To achieve this, we develop a novel probabilistic subtyping relation and merge operator, using which we prove type soundness and session fidelity. The semantics of typing contexts separates nondeterministic resolution, probabilistic choice, and synchronisation, so that every typing context induces a finite Markov decision process. On it, we derive sound lower bounds, holding under every fair adversarial scheduler, on the probability that a session is deadlock-free and live - the first behavioural property guarantees, partial or otherwise, for a probabilistic session calculus. To connect session types with probabilistic model checking, we introduce the first translation from session types into the PRISM modelling language, and prove it sound and complete with respect to our operational semantics. We implement the framework in the toolchain Prose, which translates probabilistic multiparty session typing contexts into PRISM and checks safety, deadlock-freedom, and liveness.

papers.title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Proof-step verification rewrites a solver's answer into typed steps and uses LLM judges to certify or decline. We evaluate this pipeline on open-weight models across GPQA, AIME-2025, and a MATH-500 subset. Certification raises answer-key-match precision by 31 percentage points on the strong GPQA configuration and 46 on AIME, while answering only 35% and 21% of attempts. On near-ceiling MATH-500, gains are at most 5 points at a loss of 13-27 points of coverage. An output-token-matched self-consistency selector obtains 82.9% precision at 35% coverage, compared with the verifier's pooled 87.6% (paired difference: +4.8 points, 95% interval [-8.2, 18.5]). A diagnostic sample reveals a distinct failure mode: 52 of 88 completed problems end in invalid proof construction without ever reaching a judge. Finally, external-LLM acceptance of rendered certified chains is 61.0-67.6%, compared with 87.6% answer-key match. These audits lack human or formal-kernel ground truth. Open-weight auditor pairs show near-zero chance-corrected agreement, which measures consistency rather than accuracy against proof truth. These results motivate separate reporting of execution failures, selected-answer precision, and independently assessed proof validity. We provide per-configuration results and evaluation details in the supplement.

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $Δ$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $Δ=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

papers.title: On Koebe theorem for Sobolev mappings on Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We consider mappings between domains of two Riemannian surfaces. The main subject of the investigation are families of homeomorphisms with moduli inequalities. For such families, we obtain the uniform openness (uniform lightness). As a consequence, we obtain similar results for homeomorphisms of Sobolev classes with finite distortion whenever its maximal dilatations have a majorant integrable on almost all concentric circles. In particular, we obtain the Koebe-type theorem for both direct and inverse Sobolev mappings.

papers.title: Bounding Freedom of Choice via Causal Network Embeddings
papers.abstract: Standard Bell inequalities rely on measurement independence, the assumption that measurement settings are perfectly decoupled from the source of correlations. We demonstrate that embedding Bell scenarios into larger causal networks naturally overcomes this limitation. This embedding yields experimentally accessible lower and upper bounds on measurement dependence, the incompatibility of which certifies nonclassicality directly from data, without assuming a priori freedom of choice. We formulate a general linear-programming framework to systematically derive these measurement-dependence consistency (MDC) Bell inequalities. By bypassing standard non-convexity hurdles, this approach significantly outperforms existing techniques in computational simplicity and noise robustness. Finally, we reveal that genuine quantum nonlocality can be certified even for correlations exceeding the Tsirelson bound, and demonstrate our method's broad applicability to multi-outcome and multipartite Bell tests.

papers.title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
papers.abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

papers.title: Lost in the Bins: Treatment Effects with Discretized Covariates
papers.abstract: Mean independence restrictions are widely used to identify average treatment effects, but the covariates used to formulate these restrictions are often observed or used in coarsened form. This paper shows that mean independence conditional on a finely measured covariate need not hold after the covariate is replaced by a coarsened version. Coarsening can therefore change the identifying content of the comparison rather than only the precision of estimation. I characterize the resulting coarsening bias for the ATT and ATE. For the ATT, the bias is driven by within-cell composition in untreated potential outcomes. For the ATE, an additional treatment effect heterogeneity term appears. I then introduce $c$-mean dependence, a nonparametric relaxation of exact mean independence at the coarsened level, and derive sharp bounds for average treatment effects. The parameter $c$ determines how far comparisons may extend across neighboring values of the coarsened covariate. I propose sample analogue estimators and bootstrap inference procedures for the resulting bound functions. In an application to voluntary military service using data from Angrist (1998), positive effects on early earnings, which primarily reflect military pay, hold even under the weakest form of $c$-mean dependence, whereas the evidence on later effects on civilian earnings is inconclusive once mean independence is relaxed.

papers.title: Accurate calibration method of the Back-linked Fabry Perot interferometer using null channel for space-based gravitational wave antenna
papers.abstract: Accurate calibration of the detector response is essential for precision gravitational-wave (GW) observations. In the Back-linked Fabry-Perot Interferometer (BLFPI), which employs Fabry-Perot cavities to achieve high GW sensitivity, accurate calibration of the cavity response is particularly important because residual calibration errors directly limit the suppression of laser frequency noise. However, no practical calibration strategy for the cavity response has yet been established. In this paper, we propose a method for calibrating the cavity response using a null channel constructed from the three interferometer outputs of the triangular laser-link configuration. In null channel, GW signals are canceled and residual laser frequency noise indicates errors in the cavity response estimates. Therefore we can estimate the cavity response by optimizing the response parameters to minimize the integrated power of the null channel. We derive the estimation bias introduced by technical noise analytically and evaluate the performance of the proposed method numerically. The results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed BLFPI sensitivity throughout the observation band. This demonstrates that the proposed null-channel calibration method achieves the accuracy required for effective subtraction of laser frequency noise.

papers.title: The higher order regularity problem for elliptic systems with data in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the well-posedness of the higher order regularity problem in the upper half-space with data in Sobolev Banach function spaces by proving its equivalence to natural weighted estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. The generality of our framework allows for applications to Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement-invariant spaces such as Orlicz spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, as well as their weighted counterparts, among others. This is established for the family of second-order, homogeneous, elliptic, constant complex coefficient systems in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ that admit a distinguished coefficient tensor, a natural condition that always holds in the scalar case and for the Lamé system of elasticity.

papers.title: Source Assignment: Hardness, Approximation, and Parameterized Algorithms
papers.abstract: In Source Assignment, each pointer represents a substring of a common reference string and may have several possible source occurrences. The goal is to choose one source for each pointer while minimizing the number of distinct reference boundaries used by the selected sources. The problem was introduced by Qiu and Kingsford (Bioinformatics 2021) in the context of compact genome-graph construction. We distinguish \emph{Explicit Source Assignment}, where admissible source sets are given explicitly, from \emph{Complete Source Assignment}, where all occurrences of each pointer string are available. We show that Explicit Source Assignment has an exact value-preserving formulation as cardinality Set Cover with Pairs. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, it cannot be approximated within $(1-\varepsilon)\ln p$ unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, even over a binary alphabet when all pointers have length one, while known algorithms for Minimum-Weight Multicolored Subgraph give an $O(\sqrt{q\log p})$-approximation for arbitrary pointer lengths. Our main hardness result proves that Complete Source Assignment is APX-hard even over a binary alphabet, with equal pointer lengths and at most two sources per pointer. For edge-disjoint equal-length instances, we give a $3/2$-approximation and a $1.12585$-approximation when each pointer has at most two sources. We also introduce the rainbow-path length $λ$: the problem is polynomial-time solvable for $λ\le2$, and for $λ\le3$ we obtain a $(9/8+\varepsilon)$-approximation. We further give a polynomial-time test for deciding whether abstract source sets can be realized exactly as complete occurrence sets over an unrestricted alphabet. Finally, we give exact fixed-parameter algorithms for several structural parameters, and show that Complete Source Assignment is fixed-parameter tractable in the alphabet size and maximum pointer length.

papers.title: Semiparametric Inference for Marginal Win Odds with Censored Time-to-Event Outcomes
papers.abstract: Win statistics provide clinically interpretable measures for comparing treatment groups with prioritized composite outcomes, but efficient covariate-adjustment methods for win statistics with right censored time-to-event outcomes remain limited. We develop a semiparametric framework for marginal win probability and win odds with prioritized time-to-event outcomes, including semi-competing risks, while also accommodating scalar survival outcomes as a special case. The estimand compares independent draws from the marginal distributions of the potential outcomes under treatment and control, which preserves a marginal causal interpretation. We derive the efficient influence function under conditional independent censoring, allowing censoring to depend on baseline covariates and predictable event history. The resulting cross-fitted one-step estimator incorporates covariate adjustment and censoring martingale augmentation, allows flexible estimation of nuisance parameters, and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound under suitable conditions on consistency and convergence rate of nuisance parameters. Simulation studies show that the estimator has small bias, accurate standard error estimation and confidence interval coverage, and substantial efficiency gain relative to the inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) estimator. An application to a randomized breast cancer trial comparing tamoxifen combined with radiotherapy against tamoxifen alone demonstrates improved precision, with an approximately 25\% reduction in estimated variance at five years.

papers.title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $σ$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $Σ$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = Σ\times G \to Σ$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,ω)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,Π)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = Σ\times M \to Σ$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $Σ$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,Π)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $ω$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

papers.title: A Multi-Prover Interactive Protocol for Certification of Resolution Refutations
papers.abstract: A resolution refutation of a SAT-formula $φ$ is an independently checkable certificate proving that $φ$ is unsatisfiable. However, the refutations of $φ$ can be exponentially larger than $φ$. So, a verifier needs worst-case exponential time in the size of $φ$ to check their correctness. We present ResCertify, an interactive probabilistic protocol in which the verifier interacts with multiple independent, untrusted provers (MIP) to check the refutation with very low probability of error. The verifier runs in linear time in the size of $φ$. The provers require time $\mathcal{O}(n \cdot |Φ|)$, where $Φ$ is the resolution refutation and $n$ is the number of variables of $φ$. If they can be trusted to act as a multilinear oracle on certain queries, a single prover suffices, and the runtime can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(|Φ|)$. Finally, while the focus of our work is theoretical, we also report on a proof-of-concept implementation of ResCertify.

papers.title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference weighs competing explanations of noisy data by sampling from a posterior distribution, a task that deterministic hardware performs only by simulating randomness. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) supply this randomness physically, but the few hardware networks of p-bits built so far use inorganic devices, address optimization or learning, and are judged without reference to the spread expected from finite sampling. Here we report a probabilistic computer built from solution-processed conjugated-polymer memristors. Four polymer p-bits, tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop, sample competing, degenerate and cooperative posteriors over sixteen states with statistics that fall within the range of ideal p-bits, both in their distribution and in their autocorrelation, without any parameter fitted to the target. This agreement extends to new simulated sensor readings whose outcome was predicted before each run, including readings that point away from the true answer. Reprogrammed in software, the same circuit and controller reproduces the invertible AND gate of earlier p-bit networks, with its temperature fixed in advance rather than fitted. Polymer p-bits thus open a route to printed, large-area probabilistic computers that infer alongside their sensors.

papers.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
papers.abstract: Agents that perform state estimation using pretrained perception models, e.g., Vision-Language Models (VLMs), face the fundamental challenge that predictions are uncertain. Still, most approaches determinize these predictions into a single best-guess state and make decisions as if it were ground truth. This is brittle because when the guess is wrong, the agent's decisions may be unsafe or infeasible. At the other extreme, maintaining a full probability distribution over symbolic states is often intractable. We propose a middle path, drawing on the underlying probabilities the perception model already produces (e.g., a VLM's output-layer token distributions) to construct a $θ$-confidence Minimal Belief Set (MBS$_θ$), a minimal subset of states whose cumulative probability meets a user-specified belief-mass threshold. The minimality of an MBS$_θ$ ensures that the agent considers only the most likely states, enhancing robustness in downstream decision-making while maintaining computational tractability. Using a novel three-layered belief system, we efficiently approximate individual state probabilities from per-feature predictions and task-level constraints. On this belief construction, we base our MBS$_θ$ construction, while maintaining only a lean factored representation of the belief. Our algorithm, Probability-Ranked Valid State Search (PRaVaSS), takes advantage of the unique structure of this belief system to construct an MBS$_θ$ with correctness guarantees and polynomial complexity in the unconstrained case. Using a VLM as the backbone of our state estimator, we validate our method's theoretical properties, scalability with problem size, and improvement of downstream decision-making when used in a task-planning pipeline.

papers.title: RE-PRESENT: Evidence Triangulation across Alternative Candidate-Space Views for Efficient LLM Ensemble Inference
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous large language models (LLMs) exhibit complementary strengths, motivating routing and multi-model inference methods that seek to identify reliable predictions for each input. However, exploiting this complementarity remains challenging even when a correct prediction is available within the ensemble. We investigate this challenge across heterogeneous LLM ensembles and find that a simple single-round aggregation rule is highly competitive with learned routing methods, yet substantial oracle headroom remains. Further analysis shows that the evaluated single-round response signals provide limited discriminative power for identifying reliable predictions. In contrast, controlled re-presentations of the same question elicit complementary evidence about prediction reliability. Motivated by these findings, we introduce RE-PRESENT, a training-free framework that selectively re-presents disputed questions and directly aggregates candidate-level evidence across alternative views. Across seven multiple-choice benchmarks and two heterogeneous model ensembles, RE-PRESENT improves over strong single-round aggregation while offering a favorable accuracy--cost trade-off compared with self-consistency and multi-model debate.

papers.title: Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity ($σ_c$) and normalized residual energy ($σ_r$) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, $σ_c$ shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfvén wave energy, whereas $σ_r$ displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in $σ_r$, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of $σ_r$ from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

papers.title: An Inductively Assisted N :1 Switched-Capacitor Ladder Converter
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an inductively assisted N:1 switched-capacitor ladder buck (D-SCLB) converter that replaces the output-side switch in the bottom half-bridge of an N:1 SCLB with a small inductor placed in parallel with the ladder capacitors during the demagnetization phase. The flying capacitors share the load current delivery, lowering the average inductor current to (1-M)Iout and enabling continuous regulation with M=D/(N-1+D). A closed-form output-impedance model, valid for arbitrary N under both optimal and uniform switch sizing, is derived and compared against SC, SCLB, FCMC, and DPSC topologies. For a 4:1 48V-to-PoL design, the D-SCLB reduces the average inductor current by up to 20% and improves the equivalent output impedance by up to 30% relative to the SCLB. Two hardware prototypes on a low-cost two-layer PCB achieve a peak efficiency of 96.2%, with the D-SCLB using 49% smaller inductor volume than the SCLB at comparable efficiency. Model predictions agree with measurements to within 1.5% under heavy load.

papers.title: Mach2: Scientific Discovery Platform with Deterministic Execution Constraints
papers.abstract: Language-model agents can formulate workflows and invoke specialized tools, yet compliance with natural-language operating rules is not guaranteed by prompting alone. Mach2 addresses this limitation by coupling Eigen orchestration to deterministic, lint-like checks of tool requests, source changes, acceptance tests, and artifact contracts. Domain requirements are represented as executable predicates: mandatory failures prevent advancement of the checked operation, while diagnostic findings are retained for correction or review. User-specified test-driven development (TDD), CodeGrapher's abstract-syntax-tree analysis, and history-guided evolutionary search provide complementary verification and optimization mechanisms. Mach2 also generates task-specific agent packages for execution through independently selected endpoints. The originating harness validates returned artifacts against declared interfaces and evidence requirements without assuming continuous supervision of the remote run. Model-internal-knowledge (MIK) dependencies are recorded separately from source-grounded and test-supported findings. This paper formalizes the rule-gated execution model and the agent-package lifecycle, and proposes measurable criteria for evaluating rule compliance, engineering validity, and cross-endpoint task continuity.

papers.title: SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20$μ$s, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering. We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).

papers.title: DeNA-SGN: Deterministic Neighborhood Aggregation for Verified Spiking Graph Inference
papers.abstract: Graph learning on neuromorphic substrates requires an explicit spiking realization of neighborhood aggregation, supporting control and classification. We propose DeNA-SGN, which combines fixed OR and tie-inclusive Majority aggregation of binary node features with a learned signed-weight threshold classifier. A degree-dependent inhibitory construction implements Majority through shared control neurons, enabling a complete circuit compilation into SuperNeuroMAT. Across seven datasets and 41 mapped classifiers, native simulation matches the exported ANN on every evaluated class decision and output-spike pattern. On the new confirmatory Amazon Photo dataset, DeNA-SGN achieves 83.93+-0.93% current-readout accuracy and 71.61+-2.22% strict output-spike accuracy; Wiki-CS reaches 75.99+-0.54% over 20 public masks. In the matched Cora study, we achieve 74.90+-2.67% on current-readout and 68.57+-2.94% strict spike accuracy. Complete circuit and activity accounting supports analytical energy comparisons and identifies the cost of clocking inactive neurons in large deployments. Current argmax is decoded on the host, and energy is modeled rather than measured on hardware. These findings establish a reproducible route to useful graph classification with decision-matched spiking execution and explicit implementation costs.

papers.title: An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue
papers.abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. This is costly, rewrites the language model that supplies the system's knowledge, and still leaves turn-taking either implicit or decided coarsely rather than word by word. We show that a frozen, general-purpose multimodal LLM can instead be adapted into a word-level full-duplex system with little data. Our system is a thinker-talker cascade on an 80 ms frame clock. The thinker keeps the LLM frozen and trains only lightweight adapters and a few new token embeddings (97M parameters); at every frame it emits one token of agent text, with pauses, yields, and onsets represented as tokens of the same vocabulary and kept legal by a finite-state machine. A four-stage curriculum, each stage anchored to the model's own behavior under the previous format, performs the conversion in about 30 GPU-hours. The talker reads only the thinker's discrete tokens, so the two halves are trained independently. On Full-Duplex-Bench and InteractionBench, the system is competitive with open-source full-duplex systems built through large-scale speech training: among them, it is the least likely to take the floor when the user merely pauses, backchannels most often, and leads in spoken-task accuracy, groundedness, and coherence over long conversations.

papers.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
papers.abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $ν$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}\right)^ν$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}\right)^ν$ are isomorphic if and only if $ν$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.

papers.title: Self-gravitating spinning mesonic tubes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct new self-gravitating solutions for the four-dimensional $SU(2)$ Einstein non-linear sigma model and the Einstein-Skyrme model, both minimally coupled to the Maxwell field, which describes spinning pulsed mesonic tubes. These solutions are gyratonic in the sense that they are characterized by a propagation axis and possess angular momentum. The gyratonic solutions are described by a smooth matter distribution, which is free of curvature singularities. The maximum of the energy density is concentrated on a tube around the propagation axis. We first consider the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to General Relativity and the Maxwell field, constructing asymptotically flat, spinning, pulsed gyratonic solutions. Subsequently, we include the Skyrme term in the analysis. In this case, we show that in order to maintain the resolvability of the matter field equations, the spacetime must be asymptotically de Sitter. It is also shown that, despite the fact that the total topological charge is zero, these solutions possess a non-zero topological charge density.

papers.title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
papers.abstract: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $β$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in §7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $β$. Next, it is known that the square of $β$ is isotopic to id. We reprove this by building an explicit 2-parameter family of Morse functions that trivializes the Hatcher-Wagoner family for $β^2$. We do this by utilizing exchange points and families of handle slides. In the final example, we show that another Hatcher-Wagoner family, affectionately called the double cross, also generates $β$.

papers.title: Nonlinear homogenization of periodic unit cells composed of mixed continuum and structural elements with variationally consistent boundary-member reduction
papers.abstract: Periodic architected materials may be represented by representative volume elements (RVEs) combining continuum, truss, beam, and shell constituents. Their mixed translational and rotational kinematics complicate a consistent scale transition to a macroscale Cauchy continuum. We establish a nonlinear first-order computational homogenization framework for such mixed-dimensional RVEs. An auxiliary finite-strain Cosserat continuum serves solely as a power-equivalent carrier of their virtual power and generalized boundary kinematics. Its uniform rotation is identified with the macroscopic polar rotation and its wryness vanishes, so the effective medium remains of Cauchy type. Under periodic translational and rotational constraints, the Hill-Mandel condition yields a common nodal-force virial for the effective first Piola-Kirchhoff stress, independent of element type. For lower-dimensional members on periodically identified cell boundaries, fractional ownership of internal virtual work is shown to be variationally equivalent to a topology-preserving reduction retaining one representative of each set of periodic element copies. Because this equivalence covers the complete element virtual work and consistent linearization, it applies to geometrically and materially nonlinear and path-dependent constituents without rescaling section properties, constitutive parameters, or internal variables. Numerical examples recover the analytical small-strain response and cubic symmetry of a mixed continuum-shell-beam cell, verify the reduction and discrete power balance, and demonstrate finite-rotation buckling of a hyperelastic Octet lattice and history-dependent yield-surface evolution of an elastoplastic sandwich cell. The open-source implementation abqhom couples the framework to Abaqus.

papers.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
papers.abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

papers.title: Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Periodic Solids. I. Hydrogen and p-block Elements from Boron to Chlorine
papers.abstract: We present the cc-pVXZ-s series (X = D, T, and Q) of correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for solids, covering hydrogen and the p-block elements from boron to chlorine. The series includes basis sets of consistent quality for the all-electron potential and for various pseudopotentials and effective core potentials commonly used in periodic calculations. Our design combines Dunning's construction of the molecular cc-pVXZ series with a revised material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO) algorithm for improved numerical performance. MCAO regularizes standard atomic optimization to suppress overly diffuse basis functions and ensure numerical stability in a set of reference solids. Benchmarks against standard cc-pVXZ calculations for molecules and plane-wave calculations for periodic solids establish the accuracy, transferability, and numerical stability of cc-pVXZ-s in both mean-field and correlated wavefunction calculations and confirm reliable extrapolation to the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit. As an application, we use all-electron cc-pVXZ-s to compute basis-set-converged lattice constants, bulk moduli, and cohesive energies for 7 bulk semiconductors. Using a hierarchy of correlated wavefunction methods up to local coupled cluster with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)], we find systematic convergence toward experimental bulk moduli and cohesive energies, while a small systematic overestimation of lattice constants suggests potential limitations in the approximate finite-size treatment. This work provides a foundation for the further development of systematically convergent Gaussian basis sets for periodic calculations.

papers.title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Prüfer $v$-Multiplication Domains
papers.abstract: We generalize a result known for Prüfer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

papers.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
papers.abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We find that human behavior is best captured by a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from their timing---and similarly for frontier models. However, unlike humans, none of the tested models seem to efficiently adapt their behaviors to their partners' over the course of the game. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that humans perform implicit probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals in dynamic social settings, and that such reasoning mechanisms may emerge without real-time experience. Practically, our study highlights new challenges for AI systems to coordinate efficiently with other agents by learning to interpret and adapt to their implicit signals in dynamic settings.

papers.title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
papers.abstract: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. Evaluating three models across four data-context settings shows that the benchmarks separate data contexts and model tiers. Auditing candidate queries against causal provenance in the simulation log verifies gold programs without manual annotation, including on multi-event composite tasks that expose reasoning failures in state-of-the-art agents. We hope the community uses SynthCorp to generate more challenging and useful data estates and benchmarks that foster the development of enterprise data agents.

papers.title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation. Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

papers.title: RECALL: Real-Time Recalibration of Multi-Camera Rigs via Learned OEM-Anchored Residuals
papers.abstract: Multi-camera rigs ship pre-calibrated from the manufacturer, but their calibration goes stale each time the rig is repositioned, and drifts continuously through wear, thermal cycling, and vibration. Recovering it on-the-fly is hard: classical bundle adjustment needs a fresh multi-view capture and a global optimization whose cost grows with the rig, ruling out real-time use. In this paper we present RECALL, a feed-forward method that recalibrates a movable multi-camera rig in a single pass. From the nominal OEM calibration as an anchor and a brief observation of a known object, it predicts each camera's current intrinsics and extrinsics, written as a shared global rotation of the rig composed with a small per-camera drift. Instead of regressing the calibration in one shot, RECALL refines its estimate with a learned, rig-coupled recurrent operator that reprojects through a differentiable projection and applies attention across the cameras at each step, and solves for the shared rotational gauge in-network with a learned Gauss-Newton step rather than regressing it. Because the ground truth is synthesizable, we train entirely on data generated on-the-fly and need no captured dataset. On a synthetic 10-camera benchmark, RECALL is more accurate than per-camera and rig-coupled joint bundle adjustment ($0.26^\circ$ vs $0.47^\circ$ rotation, $5.4$ vs $8.9$ px focal) and runs about $10^5\times$ faster at about $0.12$ ms per rig. On real data (TotalCapture, CMU Panoptic) it matches or beats offline rig-coupled bundle adjustment on absolute and relative rotation while running four-to-five orders of magnitude faster, and on the Panoptic surround rig it also matches the strongest image-only foundation models (VGGT, VGGT-$Ω$, $π^3$) on relative pose while staying metric and about $15\times$ more accurate in focal length. Code: https://github.com/theICTlab/RECALL-multicam
authors: Mario Alberto Tapia de la Cruz

papers.title: Open-Source Transtibial Prosthetic Bypass Preserving Joint Alignment: Gait Learning and Kinematic Evaluation
papers.abstract: Prosthetic bypasses allow able-bodied individuals to walk with a prosthesis, enabling safe early-stage testing of new prosthetic devices before clinical trials. However, existing transtibial bypasses impose constraints, such as a contralateral shoe lift or a lateral offset of the prosthesis, and their effects on gait remain poorly documented. We present an open-source transtibial prosthetic bypass that preserves part of the sagittal knee mobility without these constraints. Six able-bodied participants familiarized themselves with the bypass for approximately 10~min, then walked on a treadmill with and without it, and joint kinematics were recorded with motion capture and then extracted with OpenSim. All participants were able to walk without handrail support, although single stance remained shorter on the bypass side (27% vs. 45% of the gait cycle). Bypass-side ankle kinematics were consistent with those reported for transtibial prosthesis users, whereas peak knee flexion during swing decreased from 61° to 36° (p<0.001) and hip range of the sound leg increased from 35° to 51° (p<0.01). Although gait with the bypass does not fully replicate that of prosthesis users, it yielded consistent gait patterns after only 10~min of learning. This bypass therefore provides a useful tool for the lower-limb prosthetics research community, facilitating preliminary experiments with able-bodied participants.

papers.title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.

papers.title: Graph Label Alignment: A Diagnostic Atlas for Graph Classification
papers.abstract: Graph classification benchmarks vary widely in difficulty: some are solved by simple pooled baselines, while others remain challenging for GNNs and graph transformers. We take a data-centric view and ask whether benchmark success is driven by genuine structure--feature reasoning or by label signal already accessible from restricted marginal views. We introduce graph label alignment, a lightweight diagnostic that measures label accessibility through two supervised probes computed without training a graph encoder: structural label alignment (SLA), based on permutation-invariant topological and spectral summaries, and feature label alignment (FLA), based on pooled node features with edges removed. Across real graph classification benchmarks and multiple pooled backbones, the resulting SLA--FLA plane strongly organizes test accuracy, with low-alignment datasets forming a consistent regime where standard pooled pipelines struggle. To probe what lies beyond marginal accessibility, we introduce controlled interaction-dominated stress tests, including heterophilic ego-graphs and synthetic Twins tasks whose structural and feature marginals are matched across classes but whose role--feature couplings differ. These results show that high alignment explains much of easy benchmark performance, while low alignment reveals regimes where success requires preserving structure--feature correspondence beyond standard pooled representations.

papers.title: U.S. Data Center Growth Through 2030: A Critical Review of Grid Adequacy and Transmission Expansion Planning
papers.abstract: The growth of large data centers raises questions about both supply adequacy and the suitability of load representations used in connection studies. This paper critically reviews the U.S. demand, generation, and transmission outlook through 2030 and examines the implications for transmission expansion planning (TEP). Comparison of public forecasts highlights distinctions among annual average demand, peak demand, and grid connection capacity. National generating-capacity totals cannot establish a dependable surplus because resource availability, regional adequacy, transmission constraints, and project timing determine supply capability. Recent grid events and published dynamic studies demonstrate that faults can trigger substantial data-center transfers to backup supply, followed by delayed or coordinated demand recovery. These behaviors require appropriate representation within the conventional planning framework, alongside assessment of the requested maximum grid import. The selected literature reveals limited integration of validated data-center dynamic models into the technical screening and economic comparison of expansion alternatives. The review identifies the need to establish whether fault response and recovery change feasible connection capacity, required reinforcement, or the preferred transmission investment.

papers.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. The tasks isolate complementary capabilities, from surface-level text and Markdown extraction through summarization, classification and named-entity recognition to layout-sensitive passage and layout extraction. We evaluate 45 state-of-the-art open-weight VLMs from 1.7B to 235B parameters, plus one commercial system under the same protocol. The benchmark is far from saturated: the best average is 69.0, only eight of the 45 evaluated systems reach 65, and the two best results come from 27B models rather than from the largest systems we evaluate. Performance is uneven in ways that scale does not fix. The gap between the strongest and weakest language does not close as models grow, and it survives controlling for the domain composition of each language. Capabilities also do not improve together: once we partial out overall model quality, per-task scores are largely uncorrelated, and transcription ability in particular trades off against semantic extraction.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

papers.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
papers.abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $Δ ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\inftyλ_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $λ_n$, such that $λ_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_kλ_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

papers.title: A Sublogarithmic Competitive Algorithm for Online Graph Exploration
papers.abstract: In online graph exploration, an agent must visit every vertex of an unknown weighted graph and return to its start, learning the incident edges at each vertex it visits. On $n$-vertex graphs, the best known competitive ratio has been $O(\log n)$, achieved by several algorithms, among them the hierarchical depth-first search of Megow, Mehlhorn, and Schweitzer. We give an algorithm with competitive ratio ${(2+o(1))}\ln n/\ln\ln n$ for known~$n$. Like hierarchical depth-first search, it groups the edges into geometric weight classes and searches depth-first between components of lighter edges. Unlike it, the agent tours each component along a minimum spanning tree for the original weights, so only crossings between components pay for rounding, and the base $b$ of the weight class can grow with~$n$. The leading constant $2$ is tight for our choice of base. Without knowing $n$, restarts with increasing size guesses give upper bounds with leading constant $4$ for a fixed schedule and $2$ in expectation for a randomly shifted schedule. If the weights lie in a known range $[1,2^k]$ with $k\ge4$, choosing $b=k/\log_2 k$ gives a competitive ratio of $O(k/\log k)$ without knowing $n$.

papers.title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981. Our proof involves both human ideas and substantial AI assistance.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Hypersonic Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction Dynamics Using Plasma-Generated Disturbances
papers.abstract: The unsteady dynamics of a transitional 3D shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction (SWBLI) are investigated using pulsed plasma disturbances on a cone-slice-ramp geometry in the Boeing/AFOSR Mach-6 Quiet Tunnel.
