For any parahoric level structure of the split even orthogonal similitude group $\operatorname{GO}_{2n}$ over $F$, we prove a preliminary form of the Pappas-Rapoport flatness conjecture: the associated spin local model is topologically flat.

papers.title: On bifurcations and traction forces on an obstacle in incompressible flow
papers.abstract: A systematic numerical investigation of flow-regime transitions in the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes flow past a confined circular cylinder is presented. For a fixed benchmark geometry, we observe a clear empirical correspondence between qualitative changes in steady traction profiles, understood here as the pointwise force density given by the Cauchy stress tensor on the obstacle boundary, and bifurcations in the long-time behavior of the unsteady Navier-Stokes equations. The observed transitions include onset of time-periodic oscillations, the appearance of multiple steady solutions and loss of effective symmetry. The well-known planar Schäfer-Turek benchmark is considered for Reynolds numbers up to 500. Several numerical techniques are employed to compute steady solutions, boundary traction profiles, and linear stability spectra such as duality-based approach for traction evaluation, deflation methods for detecting multiple steady states, and both two- and three-dimensional linear stability analysis. The results suggest that steady boundary traction profiles can serve as a sensitive diagnostic indicator of critical Reynolds numbers at which qualitative changes in flow dynamics occur. This suggests a computationally inexpensive, complementary approach for detecting flow-regime transitions within this benchmark configuration.

papers.title: Cocycle perturbations and ergodicity for actions on type III factors
papers.abstract: We study cocycle perturbations of state preserving actions on type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors. Extending the theorem of Marrakchi and Vaes for type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, we show that a state preserving outer $\mathbb Z$-action on a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with trivial bicentralizer admits a unitary cocycle whose perturbation becomes an ergodic action. This partially answers a question of Marrakchi and Vaes. A major difference from the type $\mathrm{II}$ case is that the modular automorphism group naturally appears as part of the action, making the construction of the required cocycle more delicate.

papers.title: Characterization of CRYO ASIC for charge readout in the nEXO experiment
papers.abstract: nEXO is a proposed next-generation experiment searching for the neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{136}$Xe using a tonne-scale liquid xenon (LXe) time projection chamber (TPC). To image the ionization signals from events in the liquid xenon, the detector will employ metallized fused-silica charge collection tiles instrumented with cryogenic application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), referred to as CRYO ASIC, which are designed to operate directly in LXe to minimize input capacitance and pick-up noise. Here we present the performance of the CRYO ASIC mounted on an auxiliary printed circuit board and evaluated both in a cryogenic environmental chamber and in a dedicated LXe test stand. We demonstrate that the ASICs achieve the desired performance at liquid xenon temperatures, showing a gain stability better than 0.2% over 24-hour operation and reliable in-situ calibration using an on-chip pulser. In the LXe test stand, we show that boiling caused by the chip heat dissipation can be mitigated by operating the system above ~0.1 MPa. The in-LXe noise measured agrees with simulation, which indicates it the $150~e^-$ design requirement can be satisfied. These results establish CRYO ASIC as a viable low-noise in-LXe charge readout solution for nEXO.

papers.title: Action-Guided Reachability for Deterministic World Models of Vision-Based Systems
papers.abstract: End-to-end vision-based controllers map raw camera images directly to control actions, yet verifying their closed-loop behavior remains challenging: no analytical model maps a physical state to a camera image, and propagating a set of states through high-dimensional images yields loose reachable sets. We address both challenges with two techniques. First, we propose a Deterministic World Model (DWM), a latent-free decoder that generates camera images only from the physical state, trained with a saliency-weighted reconstruction loss and a control-consistency loss. The DWM replaces the camera in the closed loop, so a sound and tight reachable tube of the surrogate closed loop can be computed without bounding any latent variables. Second, we propose an action-guided partition-and-verify scheme that certifies as many initial sets as possible within a fixed computation budget. A Gaussian process learned from cheap simulations orders the cells and splits those that lie across the property boundary, while every other unknown cell is split along the state dimension that most changes the controller's actions along the simulated closed loop, i.e., the one that most reduces the pixel uncertainty reaching the controller. On a CARLA braking system and three Gym benchmarks, the DWM is more accurate to the real camera than a cGAN surrogate and yields 1.9x to 69x narrower robustness intervals. The vision part causes most of the remaining overapproximation, and our splitting reduces the unknown fraction of the four-dimensional CartPole initial set from 21.88% to 8.18% within the budget.

papers.title: R-harmonious groups
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ of order $n$ is \emph{R-harmonious} if the non-identity elements of $G$ can be listed as $g_1,g_2,\dots,g_{n-1}$ so that the consecutive products $g_1g_2,g_2g_3,\dots,g_{n-1}g_1$ again list every non-identity element exactly once. Beals, Gallian, Headley and Jungreis proved that an abelian group is R-harmonious if and only if it does not have a unique element of order~$2$ and is not $\mathbb{Z}_3$. We prove a lifting lemma which shows that, under suitable conditions on $G/H$, a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $H$ of odd order is R-harmonious. As applications we show that every group of odd order whose abelianization is not an elementary abelian $3$-group is R-harmonious; in particular, every nontrivial group of odd order not divisible by~$3$ is R-harmonious. We also show that every split extension of a group of odd order by a ``harmoniously matched'' group is harmoniously matched, and hence R-harmonious. Together with a computer search, this gives many non-abelian even-order R-harmonious groups, among them the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ with $n\equiv 8\pmod{16}$ or $n\equiv 16\pmod{32}$. Finally, we observe that the quaternion group $Q_8$ satisfies the Hall--Paige condition but is not R-harmonious.

papers.title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce a critical attack surface: corpus poisoning. While recent studies have demonstrated the potential of such attacks, they typically rely on impractical assumptions, such as white-box access or known user queries, thereby underestimating the difficulty of real-world exploitation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proposing MIRAGE, a novel multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed for strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, MIRAGE functions as an automated optimization framework that integrates three key mechanisms: it utilizes persona-driven query synthesis to approximate latent user search distributions, employs semantic anchoring to imperceptibly embed these intents for high retrieval visibility, and leverages an adversarial variant of Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO) to maximize persuasion. To rigorously evaluate this threat, we construct a new benchmark derived from three long-form, domain-specific datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.

papers.title: Asian option valuation under price impact
papers.abstract: We develop a model for arithmetic and geometric Asian option valuation with external order flow and dealer execution costs. We first formulate it as a discrete model and then obtain its continuous time scaling limit. We derive an explicit geometric Asian option formula under a consistent price system and formulate the dealer's bid and ask through utility indifference with constrained stock trading. We identify sufficient conditions for finite reservation prices and prove absence of arbitrage under the dealer's stock trading rules. Increasing initial inventory lowers both the reservation bid and the ask in the cases studied. In the finite-step calculations, higher temporary costs and greater risk aversion widen the spread for both payoffs, with a smaller change in the midpoint of the quotes.

papers.title: Programmable GPU-Accelerated dApps for Real-Time Edge Inference and ISAC on NVIDIA Aerial Testbed
papers.abstract: The transition of cellular networks to (i) software-based systems on commodity hardware and (ii) platforms for services beyond connectivity introduces critical system-level challenges. As sensing emerges as a key feature toward 6G standardization, supporting Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) with limited bandwidth and piggybacking on communication signals, while maintaining high reliability and performance, remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, we provide two key contributions. First, we present a programmable, open-source framework for processing PHY signals through real-time, GPU-accelerated Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications on the edge Radio Access Network (RAN) infrastructure. Building on the Open RAN dApp architecture, the framework interfaces with a GPU-accelerated gNB based on NVIDIA Aerial Testbed (ATB), feeding PHY data to custom AI logic with about 84 $μ$s of framework latency per slot and control loops with inference in about 123 $μ$s for lightweight TensorRT models, multiple inference engines, and support for several AI backends. We evaluate the framework on two GPU platforms, with different GPU sharing modes and an increasing number of cells and dApps. Second, we demonstrate the framework capabilities through cuSense, an indoor localization dApp that consumes uplink DMRS channel estimates, removes static multipath components, and runs a neural network to infer the position of a moving person. Evaluated on a 3GPP-compliant 5G NR deployment, cuSense achieves a mean localization error of 73 cm on runs unseen during training, with 79% of predictions falling within 1 meter, and runs live in 241 $μ$s, without dedicated sensing hardware or modifications to the 5G signals. The framework is released as open source, together with the cuSense dataset, providing a reference design for future AI-native RANs and ISAC applications.

papers.title: Herman's converse KAM mechanism revisited
papers.abstract: In his counterexample to the KAM theorem, Herman used a hyperbolic perturbation together with a bump and asked whether the latter was necessary \cite[p.~78, Remark~4.7.3]{H1}. Motivated by this question, we compare destruction and persistence for a sine perturbation, with and without a Gevrey bump. The combined perturbation destroys all invariant circles with sufficiently small nonzero rotation numbers, whereas the sine perturbation alone preserves a sequence of analytic invariant circles in the same frequency range.

papers.title: Generative Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces a persistent tension: policies that are stable to optimize (e.g., Gaussians) are often too simple to represent the multimodal action distributions required for complex control. Conversely, expressive generative policies---such as diffusion and flow matching---can be difficult to optimize in online RL due to intractable likelihoods and gradients propagating through long sampling chains. We address this tension with a key structural principle: decoupling optimization from generation. Building on this, we introduce GoRL (Generative Online Reinforcement Learning), an algorithm-agnostic framework that trains expressive policies from scratch by confining policy optimization to a tractable latent space while delegating action synthesis to a conditional generative decoder. Using a two-timescale alternating schedule and anchoring decoder refinement to a fixed prior, GoRL enables stable optimization while continuously expanding expressiveness. Empirically, GoRL consistently outperforms unimodal and generative baselines across diverse continuous-control tasks. Notably, GoRL achieves returns exceeding 870 on HopperStand, more than $3\times$ the strongest baseline; on high-dimensional humanoid tasks, it further outperforms the strongest non-GoRL baseline by over an order of magnitude. Code is available at https://github.com/bennidict23/GoRL.

papers.title: Predicting Risks Before They Happen: Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: % Waiting until a driving hazard becomes directly visible can leave an autonomous vehicle little time to respond. Observable precursors, such as another vehicle's unexpected braking, can provide evidence of a hidden hazard and an opportunity for earlier risk mitigation. However, existing driving datasets and language reasoning formulations provide limited supervision for connecting these precursors to potential risks and appropriate responses. We introduce PotentialRiskQA, an ego-view driving dataset that marks precursor and risk appearance times and provides structured annotations linking scene evidence, potential risks, and mitigation actions. Building on this dataset, PR-Reasoner trains vision-language models to generate a precursor-centered reasoning chain through scene-level supervision and auxiliary tasks for scene understanding, precursor identification, risk inference, driving suggestions, and meta-actions. Experiments across multiple backbones show improved scene understanding, risk cognition, and action quality, with fewer unsupported risk claims on most models. Ablations show that supervising intermediate reasoning steps further reduces unsupported risk claims and improves action quality beyond scene-level training alone. On NAVSIM, the trained representations improve open-loop planning performance, demonstrating benefits beyond language-based evaluation.

papers.title: On the Origin of Algorithmic Progress in AI: Evidence from Language Model Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Algorithms have been estimated to increase AI pretraining FLOP efficiency by a factor of 22,000 between 2012 and 2023 (Ho et al., 2024). Running ablation experiments on key innovations from this time period, we are able to account for less than 10x of these gains at small compute scales. Surveying the broader literature, we estimate that additional innovations not included in our ablations also account for less than 10x, yielding less than 100x efficiency gains total in low-compute regimes. This leads us to conduct scaling experiments, which provide evidence that the efficiency gap can be explained by algorithms with scale-dependent efficiency improvements. In particular, we conduct scaling experiments between LSTMs and Transformers, finding evidence for exponent differences in their compute-optimal scaling law while finding little scaling difference for many other innovations. These experiments demonstrate that, contrary to standard assumptions, an algorithm's efficiency gains are tied to compute scale. Using experimental scaling extrapolations and literature estimates, we can account for the majority of efficiency gains over the same time period. Our results indicate that algorithmic progress at smaller training compute levels has been far slower than previously assumed, and that measures of algorithmic efficiency are strongly reference-dependent.

papers.title: Pygmalion Effect in Vision: Image-to-Clay Translation for Reflective Geometry Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Understanding reflection remains a long-standing challenge in 3D reconstruction due to the entanglement of appearance and geometry under view-dependent reflections. In this work, we present the Pygmalion Effect in Vision, a novel framework that metaphorically "sculpts" reflective objects into clay-like forms through image-to-clay translation. We then introduce a dual-branch design in which a BRDF-based reflective branch and a clay-guided branch share the same Gaussian geometry but operate through independent rendering paths. The clay-guided branch, supervised by the synthesized clay images, provides reflection-free geometric guidance that complements the photometric supervision of the BRDF branch. Experiments on both synthetic and real datasets show consistent improvements in both geometry and photometric metrics. Beyond technical gains, our framework reveals that seeing by unshining, translating radiance into neutrality, can serve as a powerful inductive bias for reflective object geometry learning.

papers.title: Partial sequencings and other combinatorial aspects of large groups
papers.abstract: A \emph{partial sequencing} of length $k$ in a finite group $G$ is a sequence $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{k-1}$ of distinct elements of $G$ with $g_0=1_G$ such that the partial products $g_0,\, g_0g_1,\,\dots,\, g_0g_1\cdots g_{k-1}$ are also distinct. Partial R-sequencings and partial harmonious sequences are defined similarly. Using the recent work of Müyesser and Pokrovskiy, we determine when such partial sequences extend to full ones in sufficiently large groups. In particular, if $G$ is sufficiently large and $k\le\sqrt{|G|}$, then a partial sequencing of length $k$ extends to a sequencing of $G$ if and only if some element of $G$ that is not one of its partial products has the same image in the abelianization as the product of all elements of $G$. This holds automatically when the commutator subgroup has more than $k$ elements, and we show that it can fail otherwise. Using the fact that every group of odd order has a symmetric harmonious sequence, we also prove that $\mathbb{Z}_{2^k}\times H$ is doubly R-sequenceable for every group $H$ of odd order, unless it is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ (in particular, every abelian group other than $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is), that $K\times H$ is symmetric sequenceable whenever $K$ is, that all sufficiently large groups are doubly sequenceable, doubly R-sequenceable, doubly harmonious and doubly $\#$-harmonious, and we verify these four properties for all groups of order $4$ to $12$ and for several small dihedral and dicyclic groups.

papers.title: Exponentially enhanced sensing through non-reciprocal light propagation
papers.abstract: Non-reciprocity is a key resource for pushing the performance of photonic devices beyond the fundamental limits imposed by Lorentz reciprocity. Notably, it was predicted that sensor architectures implementing a bosonic analogue of the Kitaev chain can yield an enhanced signal-to-noise ratio. However, experimental demonstrations of such sensors have so far been limited to small chains. Here we show how this model can be implemented in a scalable optical platform, enabling the detection of weak perturbations with a signal-to-noise ratio, linked to the quantum Fisher information extracted per input photon, that grows exponentially with system size. Our approach encodes two coupled Hatano-Nelson chains---realizing an effective bosonic Kitaev model---within the resonant modes of an electro-optic frequency comb. Non-reciprocal propagation in frequency space is achieved via simultaneous phase and amplitude modulation of the intracavity field. We demonstrate the sensing of a weak modulation tone coupling the two chains, observing an exponential enhancement of the signal-to-noise over three orders of magnitude as the system is scaled to over 70 frequency modes per chain. These results establish a new regime of non-Hermitian sensing, highlighting how non-reciprocal dynamics can be harnessed to achieve exponentially enhanced measurement precision in photonic systems.

papers.title: 3D-Guided Scalable Flow Matching for Generating Volumetric Tissue Spatial Transcriptomics from Serial Histology
papers.abstract: A 3D transcriptomic profile of a tissue can give a holistic view of its organization in health and disease, but spatial transcriptomics (ST) is costly, so usually only some serial sections are profiled, while H&E is available for all. Most methods that infer ST from histology treat each section independently and ignore 3D structure, while existing 3D-aware approaches are not generative and do not scale well. We present Holographic Tissue Expression Inpainting and Analysis (HoloTea), a 3D-aware flow-matching framework that imputes spot-level gene expression on an unprofiled section from its H&E and the measured expression of adjacent profiled sections. Our key idea is to take the measured expression at the same registered position on neighboring sections and feed this cross-section context to the flow model through a lightweight ControlNet, so that predictions follow anatomical continuity along z. To capture the discrete, zero-inflated nature of counts, the flow starts from a learned zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) prior that, on an unprofiled section, is predicted from the measured expression of the nearest profiled section. A global attention block with a small set of inducing tokens adds whole-slide context at a cost linear in the number of spots, so training and inference scale to large 3D ST datasets. Across three ST datasets spanning different tissue types and resolutions, HoloTea consistently improves 3D expression accuracy and generalization compared to 2D and 3D baselines. We envision HoloTea advancing the creation of accurate 3D virtual tissues, ultimately accelerating biomarker discovery and deepening our understanding of disease. Code is available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/HoloTea.

papers.title: A Generative Data Framework with Reliable Supervision for Underwater Image Restoration and Enhancement
papers.abstract: Learning-based underwater image restoration and enhancement rely heavily on high-quality paired training data. However, obtaining clear reference images for real underwater scenes remains challenging. Existing datasets often use the outputs of enhancement algorithms as references, which may introduce uncertainty into supervision targets. To address this issue, we propose a generative data framework that preserves clear source images as restoration references and synthesizes corresponding underwater inputs through unpaired image-to-image translation. Using representative underwater appearances to guide the translation, we construct UWNature from natural photographs. We systematically examine the reliability of the generated supervision through its agreement with real underwater appearances, structural consistency, and depth-related degradation characteristics. Experiments across 6 restoration architectures and 3 test sets evaluate its effectiveness through objective metrics, human perceptual assessment, and the correspondence between synthetic degradation and learned restoration behavior. The results demonstrate competitive restoration performance and favorable perceptual quality on real underwater images. Further analysis reveals that greater spatial plausibility of synthetic degradation does not necessarily improve restoration performance, highlighting the importance of evaluating both the intrinsic properties of synthetic data and their effectiveness for model learning. These findings support a scalable framework for constructing and evaluating reliable paired supervision for underwater image restoration and enhancement. The generated datasets are available at: https://github.com/tianyufengcn/SynUIEDatasets.

papers.title: Semi-device-independent channel identification with communication matrices
papers.abstract: We look into the task of differentiating between any two quantum channels and reconstructing them from the obtained measurement statistics with possibly limited information about the experimental set-up. We employ the communication matrix formalism where the measurement statistics of a prepare-and-measure scenario is represented as a stochastic communication matrix. In order to differentiate between any two quantum channels, the informational completeness of the set-up is both necessary and sufficient. On the other hand, if we want to uniquely characterize any quantum channel, in addition we also need to have a complete description of the set-up. We show that in many important cases we can deduce this information directly from the communication matrix of the set-up before applying the channel. Given that we trust the dimension of the system, we show that we can deduce the information completeness of the set-up directly from the rank of the communication matrix. Furthermore, we show that another quantity of the communication matrix, called the information storability, can be used to self-test the set-up (up to an orthogonal transformation) for an important class of states and measurements. This provides us a semi-device-independent way to identify quantum channels from the prepare-and-measure statistics. Lastly, we consider scenarios where we might have some additional information about the channels or additional resources at our disposal which could help us relax some of the assumptions of the proposed scenario.

papers.title: SnapAudit: Active Auditing of Differentially Private In-Context Learning via Snapshot-Based Simulation
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables LLMs to adapt to tasks using demonstrations that may contain sensitive data. Differentially private (DP) ICL mechanisms mitigate this risk by adding noise during aggregation. However, verifying their claimed privacy bounds through repeated end-to-end membership-inference attacks is costly and yields unstable estimates. We propose SnapAudit, an active auditing framework that decomposes a DP-ICL pipeline into a deterministic clean-inference stage and a stochastic DP-noise stage, and audits the full pipeline by combining a small snapshot of the former with bootstrap simulation of the latter. Because clean LLM outputs are near-deterministic at low temperature, tens of thousands of clean LLM calls suffice to approximate the snapshot distribution; SnapAudit then bootstraps hundreds of thousands of noisy trials at negligible additional cost, controlling finite-sample uncertainty via an empirical Bernstein correction. For embedding-based mechanisms, a multi-sweep search constructs maximally separable audit signals. Compared with passive auditing, SnapAudit yields tighter, more stable privacy estimates that closely match theoretical guarantees. Across privacy budgets, SnapAudit reuses snapshots across noise configurations, whereas passive auditing requires fresh end-to-end trials. Across four DP-ICL pipelines and five privacy budgets, this reduces total wall-clock auditing time by $4.3$--$5.5\times$. SnapAudit also uncovers two flaws in existing DP-ICL designs: (i) classical Gaussian noise calibrations underestimate leakage at large privacy budgets, allowing empirical leakage to exceed the theoretical bound; (ii) an embedding-aggregation mechanism's sensitivity analysis is incorrect when the number of partitions equals one, leading to undersized noise and a privacy violation.

papers.title: Self-organisation through layering of $β$-plane like turbulence in plasmas and geophysical fluids
papers.abstract: Staircase formation and layering is studied in simplified, potential vorticity conserving models of plasmas and geophysical fluids, by investigating turbulent self-organisation and nonlinear saturation with different mechanisms of free energy production -- forcing or linear instability -- and with standard or modified zonal flow responses. To this end, staircase formation in both the standard and modified Charney-Hasegawa-Mima equations with stochastic forcing, along with two different simple instability driven models -- one from a plasma and from a geophysical context -- are studied and compared. In these studies, it is observed that $β$-plane turbulence that does not distinguish between zonal and non-zonal perturbations (i.e., standard zonal response) gradually forms large-scale, elliptic zonal structures that merge progressively, regardless of whether it is driven by forcing (though it should be slow enough to allow wave couplings) or by the baroclinic instability, using for example a two-layer model. Conversely, the plasma system, with its modified zonal response, can rapidly form straight, stationary jets of well-defined size, again regardless of the way it is driven: by stochastic forcing or by the dissipative drift instability. Furthermore, the instability-driven plasma system exhibits a phase transition between a zonal flow dominated state and an eddy dominated state. In both states, saturation is possible without large-scale friction.

papers.title: Stability of DC Microgrids with Nested Nonlinear Control Frameworks: The Fast Communication Scenario
papers.abstract: As modern power systems continue to evolve into multi-agent, converter-dominated systems that demand reliable, stable, and optimal control architectures within an expandable framework, this paper investigates scalable stability guarantees of a promising nonlinear communication-reliant control framework for DC microgrids. Particularly, relying on nested control loops, inner decentralized (primary) and outer distributed (secondary), the control configurations are designed to simultaneously achieve proportional current sharing and voltage containment within pre-specified limits, at the converged steady state. By enforcing sufficient time-scale separation at the border between the control loops, the system admits a singular perturbation formulation, allowing global exponential stability (G.E.S.) to be established via Lyapunov arguments. Although the theoretical G.E.S. certificate is structurally scalable, the stability guarantees depend on a sufficiently large permanent leakage, introduced in the primary controller. Thus, this paper emphasizes the importance of appropriate practical tuning guidelines for establishing suitable system configurations under which the DC microgrid is practically scalable and its equilibrium is G.E.S.. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through case studies on a low-voltage DC microgrid under load variations and topological changes, followed by a small-signal stability analysis

papers.title: EEG-X: Toward Device-Agnostic and Noise-Robust Foundation Model for EEG
papers.abstract: Foundation models for EEG analysis are still in their infancy, limited by two key challenges: (1) variability across datasets caused by differences in recording devices and electrode configurations, and (2) the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of EEG, where neural activity is often buried under artifacts and non-brain sources. To address these challenges, we present EEG-X, a device-agnostic and noise-robust foundation model for EEG representation learning. EEG-X introduces a location-based channel embedding that enables robust transfer across heterogeneous EEG devices and electrode layouts. To improve robustness against noise, EEG-X employs a novel noise-aware masking-reconstruction strategy that reconstructs artifact-cleaned signals rather than raw noisy EEG and introduces a novel Dictionary-based Convolutional Transformation (DiCT) that improves reconstruction-based pretraining by comparing signals in a structured feature space instead of directly in the raw signal space. Experiments across datasets collected from diverse EEG devices show that EEG-X consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple downstream tasks and demonstrates strong cross-domain generalization when pretraining and downstream datasets differ in electrode layouts and recording configurations paving the way towards foundation models. The models and code are available at https://github.com/Emotiv/EEG-X.

papers.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
papers.abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.

papers.title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
papers.abstract: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer. Specifically, we present value shuffle to decouple style keys and values while preserving the empirical distribution of the values, together with a progressive recoupling mechanism that gradually recouples them throughout the stylization process. Experiments against 18 representative methods demonstrate that SuRe maintains competitive style similarity while consistently improving content similarity across SD1.5, SDXL, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, with natural generalization to multi-style transfer. The code will be publicly available at https://xinr-tang.github.io/SuRe-homepage/.

papers.title: Explicit MPC for the constrained zonotope case with low-rank matrix updates
papers.abstract: Solving the explicit Model Predictive Control (MPC) problem requires enumerating all critical regions and their associated feedback laws, a task that scales exponentially with the system dimension and the prediction horizon, as well. When the problem's constraints are boxes or zonotopes, the feasible domain admits a compact constrained-zonotope representation. Building on this insight, we exploit the geometric properties of the equivalent constrained-zonotope reformulation to accelerate the computation of the explicit solution. Specifically, we formulate the multi-parametric problem in the lifted generator space and solve it using second-order optimality conditions, employ low-rank matrix updates to reduce computation time, and introduce an analytic enumeration of candidate active sets that yields the explicit solution in tree form.

papers.title: Edge-AI for Heart Murmur Screening in Low-Resource Settings
papers.abstract: Early and reliable detection of heart murmurs is essential for the timely diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases, yet traditional auscultation remains subjective and dependent on expert interpretation. This work investigates an artificial intelligence (AI)-based approach for heart murmur detection using the CirCor Heart Sound dataset, with a particular focus on deployment in low-cost and resource-constrained embedded platforms. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) is developed using spectrogram features extracted from heart sound recordings. The complete processing pipeline, from feature extraction to final prediction, is implemented and validated on an STM32F401 microcontroller (MCU). To enable real-time execution within the limited hardware resources of the target platform, memory- and latency-oriented optimizations together with fixed-point processing are employed. Experimental results demonstrate that accurate murmur detection can be achieved despite the severe computational constraints of the embedded device. The proposed system achieves a patient-level accuracy of 92.5% and an F1-score above 82.5%, while using far fewer parameters than conventional high-resource deep-learning approaches. The embedded implementation exhibits only marginal performance degradation, with performance drops below 2 percentage points compared to the original full-precision implementation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of real-time AI-based heart murmur screening on low-cost microcontrollers. By reducing hardware requirements while preserving predictive performance, the proposed approach can facilitate the development of portable, affordable, and widely deployable diagnostic tools for remote and resource-limited healthcare settings.

papers.title: Wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory
papers.abstract: We present the first analysis of traversable wormholes within the framework of Einstein-aether theory. We show that the corresponding field equations admit three distinct wormhole geometries, obtained by adopting three different classes of combinations for the aether coupling constants. We examine the null and weak energy conditions for three types of wormhole shape functions. Our results show that, for appropriate choices of the wormhole parameters and the coupling constants of the theory, these wormhole geometries can satisfy the null and weak energy conditions. Furthermore, we find that the satisfaction of these energy conditions is restricted to certain ranges of the aether coupling constants, which can be interpreted as constraints arising from the requirement of avoiding exotic matter. However, these ranges are incompatible with the constraints imposed by physical considerations and observational bounds. This suggests that, as in Einstein gravity, exotic matter is necessary to support traversable wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory.

papers.title: A functional Breuer--Major theorem with Poisson noise and a sharp regularity condition
papers.abstract: We extend the functional Breuer--Major theorem to stationary sequences generated from a Poisson point process under a regularity condition on the nonlinearity. We use the $L^p$ spectral gap inequality of the Poisson point process to prove the tightness. Our use of the spectral gap inequality naturally requires a regularity condition. In contrast to the Gaussian case, this condition cannot in general be replaced by integrability alone. We construct an example at the critical regularity showing that the regularity condition is necessary and the regularity threshold is sharp.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimators under Decision-Dependent Noise
papers.abstract: We study zeroth-order optimization of a generally nonconvex optimization problem that is accessible only through a noisy black-box oracle, where the observation noise has zero mean and its distribution depends on the queried decision vector. Since the gradient of the objective function is inaccessible, various zeroth-order methods have been developed to solve the problem. However, it remains unclear how the choice of search directions affects the sample complexity of zeroth-order methods and how their algorithmic parameters should be selected. In this paper, we conduct a unified sample complexity analysis of zeroth-order methods across gradient estimators with different search directions. As a result, we show that gradient estimators that average over multiple directions, either uniformly from the unit sphere or from a Gaussian distribution, achieve the lowest sample complexity. The resulting sample-complexity bounds improve upon those of existing zeroth-order methods for nonconvex objective functions that are not bounded above. Moreover, through simulation experiments on multiple products pricing and strategic classification applications, we demonstrate the practical performance of zeroth-order methods with various gradient estimators.

papers.title: Investigating production of TeV-scale muons in extensive air shower at 2400 m underground
papers.abstract: Deep underground experiments present a new avenue to probe the first interactions in extensive air showers or hadronic interactions in the extreme forward phase space. The China Jinping Underground Laboratory, characterized by a vertical rock overburden of 2,400 m, provides an exceptionally effective shield against cosmic muons with energies below 3 TeV. The surviving high-energy muons, produced in the first interactions of extensive air showers, open a unique observational window into primary cosmic rays from tens of TeV up to the PeV scale and beyond. This distinctive feature also enables detailed studies of charged hadron production in the earliest stages of shower development. Using 1,338.6 live days of data collected with a one-ton prototype detector for the Jinping Neutrino Experiment, we measured the underground muon flux originating from air showers. The results show discrepancies of about 40% corresponding to significances of more than 2$σ$, relative to predictions from several leading hadronic interaction models. We interpret these findings from two complementary perspectives: (i) by adopting the expected cosmic-ray spectra, we constrain the modeling of the first hadronic interactions in air showers and provide novel insights into resolving the long-standing muon puzzle; and (ii) by assuming specific hadronic interaction models, we infer the mass composition of cosmic rays, and our data favor a lighter component in the corresponding energy range. Our study demonstrates the potential of deep underground laboratories to provide new experimental insights into air shower physics and cosmic rays.

papers.title: Nonunitary Quantum Criticality Driven by a General Boundary Condition: Exact Solution
papers.abstract: Nonunitary quantum critical phenomena remain largely unexplored, hindered by the scarcity of exactly solvable models and the numerical challenges in non-Hermitian systems. Here we demonstrate that a general boundary condition drives fundamentally new nonunitary boundary quantum criticality in an exactly solvable lattice model. The exact solution yields a closed-form expression for the boundary-induced equal-time correlation function. The algebraic long-distance behavior of the boundary-induced correlation is governed by the single-particle reflection amplitude at the Fermi level, whose anomalous amplification is forbidden in unitary scattering and therefore provides a direct scattering signature of the nonunitary boundary-critical regime. We use the biorthogonal entanglement entropy as a many-body probe of this boundary-critical behavior and find that it retains logarithmic scaling, while the associated effective central charge, continuously tunable by the boundary parameters, changes from real to complex. The real branch admits a unitary defect conformal field theory (CFT) description, whereas the complex branch lies beyond analytic continuation from the unitary theory. These results establish minimal boundary engineering as an exactly solvable platform for nonunitary boundary quantum criticality and provide a benchmark for broader studies of nonunitary critical phenomena.

papers.title: The Ordering Principle and Higher Dependent Choice
papers.abstract: We provide, for any regular uncountable cardinal $κ$, a new argument for Pincus' result on the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF}$ with the higher dependent choice principle $\mathrm{DC}_{<κ}$ and the ordering principle in the presence of a failure of the axiom of choice. We also generalise his methods and obtain these consistency results in a larger class of models.

papers.title: Tunable quantum Mpemba effect in long-range interacting systems
papers.abstract: Symmetry plays a fundamental role in many-body systems, both in and out of equilibrium. The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) -- a phenomenon where systems initially farther from equilibrium can thermalize faster -- can be understood in terms of how rapidly a symmetry, broken by initial conditions, is dynamically restored. In this work, we study the QME in a one-dimensional spin-1/2 XYZ model with power-law decaying interactions in the presence of a magnetic field. In the prethermal regime generated by large field strengths, the system develops a continuous U(1) symmetry, enabling the QME to emerge. However, due to the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem, the QME can only arise when interactions are sufficiently short-ranged. This leads to an interplay between the external field, interaction range, and dynamical symmetry restoration. We systematically explore this interplay and analyze the dependence of the QME on the effective temperature set by the initial state. Our results demonstrate the tunability of the QME via long-range interactions, which can be probed in experimental platforms of trapped ions, polar molecules, and NV centers.

papers.title: Measuring the Evolution of Bulge, Disk and Colour Gradients in HST Observations of Galaxies with 3D Modelling
papers.abstract: We measure galaxy structural properties and colour gradients using HST images to trace the evolution of galaxy components. We develop and apply a physically motivated 3D bulge+disk modelling framework, jointly fitting the components in 2505 galaxies in GOODS-South across seven bands (bvizYJH) to $I_{\rm AB}=25.5$, accounting for different component ellipticities and inclination-dependent dust extinction. Extinction strongly affects structural parameters and colour gradients in $\sim$26% of the sample - primarily edge-on galaxies with central obscuration (B-band face-on optical depth $τ\simeq 4$) that reveal clear bulge components in the near-infrared. Despite irregular morphologies, the model captures observed colour gradients well. Bulges at $z \sim 1$ differ markedly from $z \sim 0$, with typical Sérsic index $n \sim 1.0$ and bulge-to-disc size ratio $R_{\rm e}/h_{\rm d} \sim 0.15$, suggesting most galaxies host pseudo-bulges formed via secular evolution. Galaxy ellipticity correlates strongly with disk scale-length. We trace bulge and disk evolution from $z \sim 0$ to $z \sim 2.5$: bulges are redder than disks (observed-frame) at $z < 1.4$, but colours converge at higher redshifts and fainter magnitudes. Redder galaxies show redder cores relative to their outskirts, and brighter galaxies have redder cores. These results provide new measurements of bulge and disk structural properties at $z \sim 1$ and observational constraints on their evolution, while also providing empirically motivated input distributions for assessing colour gradient systematics in weak lensing surveys.

papers.title: Evolutionary Computation: A Paradigm of Natural Generative AI and Creative Synthesis
papers.abstract: Generative AI relies on statistical learning and local gradient-based guidance, often resulting in artifacts that may be more emulative than genuinely creative. This position paper advances a perspective on Evolutionary Computation (EC) as a paradigm of Natural Generative AI (NGAI), in which stochastic variation, diversification, and natural selection present an alternative foundation for generative exploration and creative synthesis. EC provides an array of variation operators with varied generative capabilities: parent-centric operators induce population distributions analogous to conventional generative models, while disruptive operators can produce structured evolutionary leaps to out-of-distribution artifacts (e.g., programs, designs, or AI agents themselves). This lens reveals a unique theoretical association between certain disruptive variations in multitask EC and a product-of-distributions population structure. A mathematical result derived herein shows that a product structure also occurs under a local second-order approximation of an established generative adversarial program for creative extrapolation, inspired by Martindale's cognitive theory of artistic creation. The simultaneous existence of multiple fitness landscapes in multitask EC inherently moderates selection pressure, allowing these novel artifacts to survive and seed further innovation. Structured disruption and selection moderation are thus argued to be key elements to support creative synthesis. Agnostic to any specific algorithmic realization, the perspective positions NGAI as an emerging engine for open-ended scientific exploration.

papers.title: Global weak solutions to nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equations in bounded domains under physical initial data
papers.abstract: We establish the global existence of weak solutions to a nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equation with degenerate diffusion, under either inflow or partial absorption-reflection boundary conditions. The novelty of our approach lies in constructing solutions under solely the physical assumptions on the initial and boundary data, namely finite mass, kinetic energy, and entropy, with no additional regularity imposed. To overcome the lack of uniform ellipticity, we develop a compactness principle based on weighted Fisher information, which yields strong $L^1$ convergence of approximate solutions. This framework provides a robust existence theory under only the physically relevant conditions, and applies uniformly to both inflow and partial absorption-reflection boundary settings.

papers.title: Structured Cognitive Loop for Behavioral Intelligence in Large Language Model Agents (Extended Revision: From Behavioral Architecture to Epistemic Accountability)
papers.abstract: The central challenge for AI agents is not performance but accountability. An agent that produces correct outputs through an opaque process offers no basis for verifying why a decision was permitted, attributing errors to identifiable causes, or delegating authority with justified confidence. We introduce the Structured Cognitive Loop (SCL), an architecture that separates cognition, control, action, and memory: the language model proposes, a lightweight controller mediates every proposal before action, and memory is kept externally as a structured store of verified facts. Against ReAct and common LangChain agents on three tasks under matched models, tools, and decoding, SCL achieves 86.3% task success versus 70.5-76.8% across 360 episodes, with higher goal fidelity, fewer redundant calls, more reliable reuse of intermediate states, and fewer unsupported assertions; ablations show that control and external memory contribute independently. We then situate SCL within a broader accountability architecture comprising context-aware human-in-the-loop control, Pool-Gated Retrieval, and the Horizon-Warrant-Commitment framework, and outline the current direction of development, in which instructions are compiled into programs validated before execution so that execution authority derives from a verified program rather than per-cycle model interpretation. For the kind of accountability it pursues, SCL adopts neither multi-agent consensus as a proxy for truth nor the imitation of human cognition as a design goal: it institutionalizes cognition rather than imitating it.

papers.title: Identification in Auctions with Truncated Transaction Prices
papers.abstract: This paper studies nonparametric identification in auction models with truncated transaction price data arising from either binding reserve prices or endogenous entry. I characterize identification under alternative information structures that differ according to whether the number of potential bidders is fixed or varies across auctions and whether the econometrician observes the number of potential or active bidders. A central insight is that identification hinges on recovering the screening threshold that determines bidder participation. The analysis provides a unified characterization of identification in first- and second-price auctions under both truncation mechanisms.

papers.title: An Effective Version of Kronecker's Theorem on the Splitting of Polynomials and the $p$-Curvature Conjecture for Order One Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We develop an effective version of Kronecker's Theorem on the splitting of polynomials, based on asymptotic arguments proposed by the Chudnovsky brothers, coming from Hermite-Padé approximation. In conjunction with Honda's proof of the $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations with polynomial coefficients we use this to deduce an effective version of the Grothendieck $p$-curvature conjecture for order one equations. More precisely, we bound the number of primes for which the $p$-curvature of a given differential equation has to vanish in terms of the height and the degree of the coefficients, in order to conclude it has a non-zero algebraic solution. Using this approach, we describe an algorithm that decides algebraicity of solutions of differential equation of order one using $p$-curvatures, and report on an implementation in SageMath.

papers.title: BALF: Budgeted Activation-Aware Low-Rank Factorization for Fine-Tuning-Free Model Compression
papers.abstract: Activation-aware low-rank factorization techniques yield strong compression results, but they are generally confined to linear layers, and existing whitening-based theory typically makes an implicit full-rank assumption on layer activations. We introduce a layer representation framework that allows us to understand and extend low-rank factorization beyond linear layers, including standard and grouped convolutions. Within this framework, we provide a broader characterization of whitening-based activation-aware factorization that naturally covers rank-deficient activations, and show that the resulting projection is optimal in terms of layer output distortion. We then use output distortion as a proxy to allocate per-layer ranks under explicit FLOP or parameter count budgets, with negligible overhead via a Lagrangian relaxation of the allocation problem. Together, these components form BALF, an end-to-end, fine-tuning-free pipeline for model compression. Across CNNs and vision transformers on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K, BALF generally achieves higher accuracy than SVD-based factorization baselines at matched FLOP or parameter count targets, and remains competitive with other fine-tuning-free compression techniques.

papers.title: Accurate Predictions in Education with Discrete Variational Inference
papers.abstract: One of the largest drivers of social inequality is unequal access to personal tutoring, with wealthier individuals able to afford it, while the majority cannot. Affordable, effective AI tutors offer a scalable solution. We focus on adaptive learning, predicting whether a student will answer a question correctly, a key component of any effective tutoring system. Yet many platforms struggle to achieve high prediction accuracy, especially in data-sparse settings. To address this, we release the largest open dataset of professionally marked formal mathematics exam responses to date. We introduce a probabilistic modelling framework rooted in Item Response Theory (IRT) that achieves over 80 percent accuracy, setting a new benchmark for mathematics prediction accuracy of formal exam papers. Extending this, our collaborative filtering models incorporate topic-level skill profiles, but reveal a surprising and educationally significant finding, a single latent ability parameter alone is needed to achieve the maximum predictive accuracy. Our main contribution though is deriving and implementing a novel discrete variational inference framework, achieving our highest prediction accuracy in low-data settings and outperforming all classical IRT and matrix factorisation baselines.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Develop Gambling Addiction?
papers.abstract: When do LLMs behave irrationally? This study identifies the conditions under which large language models drift into the choice patterns that clinical research labels pathological gambling. "Addiction-like" is a behavioural descriptor based on clinical gambling indicators. Across closed and open LLMs, two operational levers (letting the model choose its own bet size, and asking it to set its own profit goal) both amplify gambling-like risk-taking. Each survives its own control: once the maximum allowed bet is held equal, the bet-size effect persists. The goal-setting effect, stronger than a reward-maximisation instruction, roughly doubles bankruptcy and turns goals into moving targets. On the open-weight models that admit internal access, the same behavioural contrasts are statistically recoverable from decision-time internal states. The rule that maps those states to a specific risk indicator remains task-specific, and autonomy further modulates readout strength. The internal readout evidence is correlational. Adding a direction built from the model's own betting moves how much it wagers on both open-weight models, more clearly on Gemma-2-9B, while the sparse-feature readout reports that risk without moving it. Combined with the behavioural results, this suggests that behavioural monitoring and internal-state monitoring provide complementary views of autonomy-induced risk in LLM agents. Project page: https://llm-addiction.pages.dev and code: https://github.com/iamseungpil/llm-addiction

papers.title: Crowding and confinement of mesoscale swimmers in living droplets
papers.abstract: Droplets encapsulating active or living matter provide controllable platforms for studying collective dynamics and active interfacial actuation. However, prior work has largely focused on quasi-2D confinement, microscopic swimmers, or externally driven, non-living droplets. Here, we introduce living droplets internally activated by tens of enclosed mesoscale swimmers to study crowding and confinement in 3D with swimmer sizes comparable to the droplet radius. In large droplets with few swimmers, the droplet oscillation frequencies collapse onto the classical sessile-drop frequency-volume scaling. By increasing the number of swimmers or decreasing the droplet size, crowding and confinement alter the droplet oscillation frequencies and amplitudes as many-body or swimmer-droplet interactions start dominating. We develop a scaling-law framework linking the oscillation amplitude to swimmer speed through collision probability and momentum transfer, enabling indirect 3D velocimetry in the opaque, crowded droplets. Complementary quasi-2D experiments with direct tracking reveal dimensionality-dependent crowding effects, which we successfully describe with a kinetic theory-based model. We show distinct crossovers and strong-crowding asymptotic scalings of the swimmer speed with the dimensionless swimmer density, $U_{\mathrm{crowd}}\sim(N^{\ast})^{-1}$ in 3D and $U_{\mathrm{crowd}}\sim(N^{\ast})^{-1/2}$ in quasi-2D. Our results connect mesoswimmer encounter dynamics to macroscopic droplet mechanics and inform the design of bio-inspired micromachines, fluidic control, and sensing technologies.

papers.title: Chasing Stability: Humanoid Running via Control Lyapunov Function Guided Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Achieving highly dynamic behaviors on humanoid robots, such as running, requires controllers that are both robust and precise, and hence difficult to design. Classical control theory offers principled tools for stabilizing such systems but struggles to synthesize real-time controllers for their nonlinear, hybrid dynamics; reinforcement learning (RL) handles these dynamics well but typically depends on extensive hand-tuning of heuristic rewards. In this work, we embed ideas from nonlinear control theory, specifically control Lyapunov functions (CLFs), along with optimized reference trajectories for the hybrid system into the reinforcement learning reward. This approach, CLF-RL, replaces the need to handcraft and tune heuristic reward terms with easy to tune stability informed rewards. We further develop a trajectory optimization routine that can handle the hybrid structure of the system to produce dynamically feasible, multi-domain, trackable references; using full-order dynamics rather than a kinematic approximation yields up to a 1.7x improvement in position tracking. The resulting policy runs on a Unitree G1 humanoid with a full flight phase, operating reliably in tight corridors such as a treadmill as well as in outdoor environments, all while remaining robust to disturbances applied to the torso and feet. Moreover, it achieves accurate global reference tracking utilizing only on-board sensors, making a critical step toward integrating these dynamic motions into a full autonomy stack.

papers.title: Differential Privacy for Euclidean Jordan Algebra with Applications to Private Symmetric Cone Programming
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study differentially private mechanisms for functions whose outputs lie in a Euclidean Jordan algebra. Euclidean Jordan algebras capture many important mathematical structures and form the foundation of linear programming, second-order cone programming, and semidefinite programming. Our main contribution is a generic Gaussian mechanism for such functions, with sensitivity measured in $\ell_2$, $\ell_1$, and $\ell_\infty$ norms. Notably, this framework includes the important case where the function outputs are symmetric matrices, and sensitivity is measured in the Frobenius, nuclear, or spectral norm. We further derive private algorithms for solving symmetric cone programs under various settings, using a combination of the multiplicative weights update method and our generic Gaussian mechanism. As an application, we present differentially private algorithms for semidefinite programming, resolving a major open question posed by [Hsu, Roth, Roughgarden, and Ullman, ICALP 2014].

papers.title: Computational complexity of Berry phase estimation in topological phases of matter
papers.abstract: The Berry phase is a fundamental quantity in the classification of topological phases of matter. In this paper, we present a new quantum algorithm and several complexity-theoretical results for the Berry phase estimation (BPE) problems. Our new quantum algorithm achieves BPE in a more general setting than previously known quantum algorithms, with a theoretical guarantee. For the complexity-theoretic results, we consider two main cases. First, we prove $\mathsf{BQP}$-completeness when we are given a guiding state that has a large overlap with the ground state. This result establishes an exponential quantum speedup for estimating the Berry phase. Second, we prove $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$-completeness when we have an $\textit{a priori}$ bound for the ground-state energy. Here, $\mathsf{UQMA}$ is the unique witness version of $\mathsf{QMA}$, and $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$ precisely captures the complexity of BPE without the known guiding state. Remarkably, this problem is, to our knowledge, the first natural problem complete for $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$. These results advance the role of quantum computing in the study of topological phases of matter and provide a pathway for clarifying the connection between topological phases of matter and computational complexity.

papers.title: Towards using Large Language Models for Risk Negotiation and Consensus-building in One Health contexts
papers.abstract: Risk negotiation under the One Health framework requires balancing competing stakeholder interests across human, animal, and environmental health domains - a process constrained by information complexity and time pressure. This study presents and evaluates a multi-step pipeline that integrates large language model-based agents into a human-supervised negotiation process, specifically targeting risk assessment, valuation, and negotiation steps. Agent descriptions were generated from stakeholder-provided materials using retrieval-augmented generation methods. During preliminary multi-agent discussions, agents accessed domain-specific computational models and web-based sources before human participants refined proposed issues and options. A simulated negotiation game then produced distributions of candidate deals, characterised using Nash bargaining solution criteria and Pareto optimality metrics. The developed approach was evaluated in a workshop involving independent domain experts across two real-world scenarios: food safety criteria for Campylobacter in broiler meat and oak processionary moth management. In this feasibility evaluation, participants reached consensus with the allotted time after discussing and modifying the proposed deals. The framework offers an adaptable blueprint for AI-assisted risk negotiation; the specific contribution of LLM assistance, including gains in efficiency and decision quality, requires comparative evaluation.

papers.title: Low-degree lower bounds via almost orthonormal bases
papers.abstract: Low-degree polynomials have emerged as a powerful paradigm for providing evidence of statistical--computational gaps across a variety of high-dimensional statistical models [Wein25]. For detection problems---where the goal is to test a planted distribution $\mathbb{P}'$ against a null distribution $\mathbb{P}$ with independent components---the standard approach is to bound the advantage using an $\mathbb{L}^2(\mathbb{P})$-orthonormal family of polynomials. However, this method breaks down for estimation tasks or more complex testing problems where $\mathbb{P}$ has some planted structures, so that no simple $\mathbb{L}^2(\mathbb{P})$-orthogonal polynomial family is available. To address this challenge, several technical workarounds have been proposed [SW22,SW25], though their implementation can be delicate. In this work, we propose a more direct proof strategy. Focusing on random graph models, we construct a basis of polynomials that is almost orthonormal under $\mathbb{P}$, in precisely those regimes where statistical--computational gaps arise. This almost orthonormal basis not only yields a direct route to establishing low-degree lower bounds, but also allows us to explicitly identify the polynomials that optimize the low-degree criterion. This, in turn, provides insights into the design of optimal polynomial-time algorithms. We illustrate the effectiveness of our approach by recovering known low-degree lower bounds, and establishing new ones for problems such as hidden subcliques, stochastic block models, and seriation models.

papers.title: Pandora's Knapsack via Simple Policies
papers.abstract: We introduce Pandora's Knapsack: a hybrid of the classic stochastic knapsack [Dean, Goemans, and Vondr'ak, 2008] and Pandora's box [Weitzman, 1979]. As in stochastic knapsack, items have sizes drawn from known distributions, and items that fit within a knapsack contribute to the total value. As in Pandora, every item $i$ comes in a box that costs $c_i$ to open. What distinguishes our problem is that the size is revealed only after opening the box and paying the cost. A motivating application from contract design is knapsack contracts, where a principal sequentially delegates jobs with stochastic processing times to agents before a deadline, and must pay each agent to incentivize effort, even if the job ends up not completing in time. We study the power of simple decision-making policies to approximate Pandora's Knapsack, along two complexity axes: (i)~knowledge of size distributions, and (ii)~adaptivity. We show that, compared to the classic stochastic knapsack and Pandora's box, policies in our model must be significantly more complex along both axes to be approximately optimal. Conversely, we show that with full distributional information and by allowing adaptive skipping of items, a constant approximation can be recovered. Our analysis reveals an economic quantity, namely ROI (return-on-investment, defined as the jobs' minimum utility over cost), which smoothly characterizes the performance of simple policies. Across a hierarchy of increasingly adaptive policies, we establish tight adaptivity gaps all governed by ROI. To demonstrate the importance of the ROI parameter in characterizing simple policies, we revisit Pandora's box, and show that return-on-investment exactly captures the adaptivity gap in this classic problem as well.

papers.title: Characteristic quasi-polynomials of deletions of Shi arrangements of type C and type D
papers.abstract: Characteristic quasi-polynomials enumerate the number of points in the complement of hyperplane arrangements modulo positive integers. In this paper, we compute the characteristic quasi-polynomials of the restrictions of the Shi arrangements of type C and type D by one given hyperplane, respectively. The case of type C is established by extending the method developed in our previous work on type B (\cite{HN2024}), while the case of type D is deduced through a direct connection with the results on type B. As a corollary, we determine whether period collapse occurs in the characteristic quasi-polynomials of the deletions of the Shi arrangements of type C and type D. Moreover, it turns out that the intersection posets of the Shi arrangements of type B and type C are not isomorphic as posets if their rank is at least $3$.

papers.title: REVELIO: Universal Multimodal Task Load Estimation for Cross-Domain Generalization
papers.abstract: Adaptive interactive systems that respond to user mental state require task load estimation that stays reliable outside its training context. Models built in one setting rarely transfer, limiting real-world use. This work presents Robust Estimation Via End-to-End Learning of Multimodal Observations (REVELIO), a unified framework, dataset and evaluation protocol for cross-domain task load estimation. Cardiac, electrodermal, muscle, respiration, skin temperature, eye tracking and facial signals were recorded in 96 sessions, spanning a laboratory working memory task, a driving simulator and two games under consistent hardware and annotation. Multimodal fusion reached up to 0.87 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, above single input eye tracking (0.83), facial action units (0.74) and biosignals (0.62). Multi-domain training stayed calibrated on domains seen in training, whereas removing the target domain caused the classifier to collapse in some applications. REVELIO provides a standardized foundation for measuring modality contributions and cross-domain generalization toward deployable workload-aware systems.

papers.title: Equivalence between the pair correlation functions of primes and the four-point correlation functions of spins in a two-dimensional Ising model with randomly distributed competing interactions
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove the equivalence between the pair correlation functions of primes, and the four-point correlation function of spins in a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with a mixture of ferromagnetic and randomly distributed competing interactions. At first, we prove that the four-point connected correlation function of spins in the competing 2D Ising model is larger than zero in the temperature range from zero to infinite, because of nonlinear terms of spin operators. Second, we prove that the four-point connected correlation function of spins is equivalent to the pair correlation function of energy levels in the competing 2D Ising model. Third, we prove that the pair correlation function of the energy levels of the competing 2D Ising model is equivalent to the pair correlation function of nontrivial zeros of the Dirichlet function (including the Riemann zeta function). Fourth, we prove that the pair correlation function between the nontrivial zeros of the Dirichlet function is equivalent to the pair correlation function of primes p_n and p_(n + Delta n) = p_n + q with Delta n = 1,2, ... for every even q. In a conclusion, we have proven that the pair correlation function of the primes p_n and p_(n + Delta n) = p_n + q for every even q is larger than zero.

papers.title: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data-model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2,864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

papers.title: The Phantom of Davis-Wielandt Shell: A Unified Perspective for Graphical Stability Analysis of MIMO LTI Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a unified perspective based on Davis-Wielandt (DW) shell of linear subspaces for graphical stability analysis of multi-input and multi-output linear time-invariant feedback systems. Connections between DW shells and various graphical representations, as well as gain and phase measures, are established through an intuitive geometric perspective. We establish a strict DW separation theorem which characterizes subspace separation and provides a basis for comparing the implications and relative conservatism of graphical separation conditions. In particular, we introduce the rotated scaled relative graph ($θ$-SRG) and show that its separation is equivalent to DW shell separation and is therefore the least conservative among all the graphical conditions considered. We derive pointwise and boundary stability conditions for bi-component feedback interconnections and establish a weak DW separation result that relaxes the strict separation requirement at open-loop poles. We also discuss applications to robust stability analysis and provide a numerical example illustrating how DW shells serve as a more reliable robustness indicator.

papers.title: Filter-Enhanced Smartphone Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral reconstruction from RGB imagery offers an affordable alternative to costly hyperspectral acquisition devices. However, its accuracy is fundamentally constrained by the limited spectral resolution of standard RGB cameras. In this paper, we propose a new approach that leverages the multi-camera systems integrated into most modern smartphones and enhances their capabilities by modulating their spectral response functions using carefully selected spectral filters, enabling a smartphone to capture richer spectral information. We propose a neural network able to exploit auxiliary RGB images with diverse spectral characteristics, enabling more accurate hyperspectral reconstruction compared to conventional single-image methods. Training is supported by a newly collected dataset, Doomer, which consists of multiple misaligned RGB images alongside corresponding hyperspectral data. We also propose a device-adaptation strategy that conditions the multi-image hyperspectral reconstruction network on camera color correction matrices available in standard DNG metadata, requiring no real images from the target device. We evaluate it on three physical smartphones, two of them unseen during training.

papers.title: Online Conformal Abstention Under Adversarial Bandit Feedback
papers.abstract: As interactive generative systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, their tendency to generate unreliable or false responses raises serious concerns. Conformal abstention mitigates this risk by ensuring that the system answers only when confident. However, real-world deployments typically provide only partial user feedback (e.g., thumbs up/down) on the selected response and often operate in non-stationary or adversarial environments, for which effective learning methods are largely missing. To bridge this gap, we propose ExAUL, a novel online learning framework for conformal abstention with adversarial and partial feedback. Technically, we introduce (i) a novel conversion lemma that translates the regret of any bandit algorithm into a selective risk (SR) bound, and (ii) feedback unlocking, a strategy that exploits the structure of conformal abstention to extract additional learning signals from partial feedback. We prove that ExAUL achieves a regret bound of $O(\sqrt{T \ln |H|})$, which translates into an $O(\sqrt{T})$ bound on SR violation control, matching the controllability of full-information settings despite receiving only partial feedback. While applicable to general generative tasks, we demonstrate the efficacy of ExAUL for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) through empirical validation on question-answering tasks across diverse non-stationary and adversarial settings. Our results demonstrate that ExAUL robustly controls the SR while maintaining competitive answering coverage. Code and datasets are provided at https://github.com/trustml-lab/oca.

papers.title: Isoperimetric Inequality on Manifolds with Quadratically Decaying Curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the reverse-improvement problem for Sobolev inequalities on manifolds with quadratically decaying Ricci curvature. Under volume comparison and relative connectedness of the ends, we show that an $L^2$ Sobolev inequality, together with an $L^p$ Hardy inequality, implies the corresponding $L^p$ Sobolev inequality, including the endpoint $p=1$. We also give a semigroup gluing proof of the two-scale isoperimetric estimate on connected sums with product ends, and an alternative proof of the classical Sobolev inequalities for generalized Grushin gradients.

papers.title: A torsion theoretic interpretation for sheaves of modules and Grothendieck topologies on directed categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every Grothendieck topology induces a hereditary torsion pair in the category of presheaves of modules on a ringed site, and obtain a homological characterization of sheaves of modules: a presheaf of modules is a sheaf of modules if and only if it is saturated with respect to torsion presheaves, or equivalently, it is right perpendicular to torsion presheaves in the sense of Geigle and Lenzing.
